title: Derived Mayer-Vietoris triangle for native adic direct image
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], with its extended absolute-value topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], on a small representative of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $B_T(W)$ be the continuous functions $|W|\to\Omega$ whose values locally span a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector space, with restrictions by precomposition, and put $\mathcal A(T)=\operatorname{Mod}(B_T)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a scheme morphism $g:T\to S$, use the ordinary sheaf direct image with its $B_S$-action induced by precomposition $B_S\to g_*B_T$, and its total right derived functor $Rg_*$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-open-immersion], write $j^*$ for restriction of module sheaves to $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and also for its termwise functor on derived categories; here $B_T|_U=B_U$. Let $T=U\cup V$ be a cover by two open subschemes, let $W=U\cap V$, let $j_U,j_V,j_W$ denote their inclusions into $T$, and let $g:T\to S$ be any scheme morphism. For every $C\in D(\mathcal A(T))$ there is a distinguished triangle in $D(\mathcal A(S))$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]
$$Rg_*C\longrightarrow R(gj_U)_*(C|_U)\oplus R(gj_V)_*(C|_V)\longrightarrow R(gj_W)_*(C|_W)\longrightarrow (Rg_*C)[1].$$
Here the first map is the pair of restriction maps induced by the open adjunction units, and the second map is restriction from $U$ minus restriction from $V$. No finiteness or constructibility hypothesis is imposed on $C$ or $g$.

proof.text: For $Z=U,V,W$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1) identifies $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/Z$. Under this equivalence $B_T|_Z=B_Z$: on an object $P\to Z$, both rings consist of the same locally finite-dimensional continuous functions on $|P|$, with the same operations and restriction maps. This uses the displayed definition of $B$, not the constant-coefficient clause of the localization lemma. Restriction is exact by [lem-sfb-ringed-site-restriction-kflat], so it preserves cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms; its termwise functor therefore represents the restriction on derived categories. Iterated restrictions are sectionwise identities by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Work throughout in a common universe in which these sites are small and coefficient values belong to the module universe.

source.place: Restriction to a localized ringed site; lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open and the localization discussion preceding it; coefficient identification written out by Q32

proof.text: For an open inclusion $j:Z\hookrightarrow T$, ordinary direct image is $(j_*N)(P)=N(P\times_T Z)$, with scalars restricted along $B_T(P)\to B_Z(P\times_T Z)$. The restriction adjunction can be checked directly: a map $\psi:M|_Z\to N$ gives the map $M(P)\to M(P\times_T Z)\xrightarrow{\psi}N(P\times_T Z)$; conversely evaluate a map $M\to j_*N$ on objects over $Z$, where $P\times_T Z=P$. These operations are inverse by naturality. Thus $j^*\dashv j_*$ has unit the ordinary restriction maps and counit the identity under that identification. The same calculation for nested opens gives the restriction $j_{Z*}(M|_Z)\to j_{W*}(M|_W)$ when $W\subseteq Z$. All these maps are linear by the sectionwise module definition [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and the identities remain true degreewise for complexes and modulo homotopies.

source.place: Localization of ringed sites, Section 03DH; explicit verification of the open restriction/direct-image adjunction

proof.text: Represent $C$ by a complex $K$ and choose $K\to I$ K-injective with every $I^n$ injective, using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] for the small ringed site $(T_{\mathrm{proet}},B_T)$. Thus $QI\cong C$. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], $I_Z=I|_Z$ is K-injective for $Z=U,V,W$. Its universe requirement is met by regarding site objects, arrows and ring values in the common enlarged universe fixed in step 1. Restriction sends zero maps to zero sectionwise. By exactness from [lem-sfb-ringed-site-restriction-kflat], $K|_Z\to I_Z$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $QI_Z\cong C|_Z$. No truncation of $K$ or $I$ has been made.

proof.text:
Define complexes on $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by $A=g_*I$, $D=(gj_U)_*I_U\oplus(gj_V)_*I_V$ and $E=(gj_W)_*I_W$. Define $a:A\to D$ by the pair of restrictions and $b:D\to E$ by restriction from $U$ minus restriction from $V$. To check exactness in degree $n$, take any $P\to S$ in $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $P_T=P\times_S T$, and put $P_Z=P_T\times_T Z$. Base-change stability in [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change] makes all these objects of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], $P_U,P_V$ are open subschemes of $P_T$; their underlying opens are inverse images of $U,V$, so they cover $P_T$, hence a covering in the pro-etale topology [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and its overlap is $P_W$. The sheaf axiom gives injectivity and exactness in the middle of
$$0\to I^n(P_T)\xrightarrow{(r_U,r_V)}I^n(P_U)\oplus I^n(P_V)\xrightarrow{r_{UW}-r_{VW}}I^n(P_W)\to0.$$
The arrow $P_W\to P_U$ is a monomorphism: an arrow to an open subscheme is unique when it exists, as in [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](4). By [lem-pur-ringed-site-injective-mono-restriction], $I^n(P_U)\to I^n(P_W)$ is surjective. Given $c$ in the last group, lift it to $x$ in $I^n(P_U)$; then $b(x,0)=c$. The displayed sequence is therefore exact at every section. Its maps are $B_S(P)$-linear, and restrictions commute with $d_I$. Kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; thus $0\to A\xrightarrow a D\xrightarrow b E\to0$ is degreewise short exact in $\mathcal A(S)$.

proof.text:
All four direct-image functors used in step 4 are additive: they act on sections and on addition of morphisms by precomposition, with the stated scalar restriction. Their sources admit K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The comparison of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], whose existence and computation are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], therefore identifies
$$QA\cong Rg_*C,\quad QD\cong R(gj_U)_*(C|_U)\oplus R(gj_V)_*(C|_V),\quad QE\cong R(gj_W)_*(C|_W).$$
For the first use $I$; for the other three use $I_U,I_V,I_W$ from step 3. These are unbounded K-injective computations, not an assertion that a merely termwise injective unbounded complex computes a derived functor. The middle identification also uses additivity of the localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so it preserves the finite biproduct.

Check the normalization of the first map. For $j=j_U$ or $j_V$, the exactness of $j^*$ and the adjunction of step 2 imply that $j_*I_Z$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. The bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] applied to the K-injective targets $I_Z$ and $j_*I_Z$ turns the degreewise adjunction into
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B_T)}(QN,Q(j_*I_Z))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B_Z)}(Q(N|_Z),QI_Z).$$
The identity of $QI_Z$ corresponds to $Q(I\to j_*I_Z)$, since its chain-level transpose is the identity of $I_Z$. Hence this is the canonical derived open adjunction unit at $QI$. Both $I$ and $j_*I_Z$ are K-injective. Naturality of the derived comparison in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] says that applying $Rg_*$ to this map is represented by $g_*(I\to j_*I_Z)$. Finally $g_*j_*I_Z=(gj)_*I_Z$ sectionwise, including the coefficient action, since precomposition of functions is associative. Using this same complex for both derived computations identifies $Q(a)$ with the pair of required restriction maps; it does not choose an arbitrary comparison isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 08BJ, 070I and 070Y: adjoint-preserve-K-injectives, K-injective Hom bijection and normalized derived computation; explicit transpose calculation

proof.text: For $k:W\hookrightarrow Z$, $Z=U,V$, repeat step 6 on $Z$ with $I_Z$ and $I_W$: the underived unit is the restriction to $W$, $k_*I_W$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies its transpose with the identity. Naturality of the comparison [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] computes its image under $R(gj_Z)_*$ by the degreewise restriction map. The two termwise composites $(gj_Z)_*k_*I_W=(gj_W)_*I_W$ agree, with the same coefficient action. Thus $Q(b)$ is precisely restriction from $U$ minus restriction from $V$. There is no extra sign in either restriction: on sections $b(x,y)=x|_{P_W}-y|_{P_W}$, so $ba$ is zero because the two restrictions of any section coincide.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to the degreewise short exact sequence of step 4 in the abelian category $\mathcal A(S)$. It gives a distinguished triangle $QA\xrightarrow{Q(a)}QD\xrightarrow{Q(b)}QE\to QA[1]$. Transport it along the isomorphisms of step 5 and their shifts. Being distinguished is invariant under an isomorphism of triangles [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Steps 6 and 7 identify the first two arrows, including the minus sign, so this is exactly the triangle in the statement. The argument used only smallness, module sheaf gluing, injective terms and K-injectivity; it imposed no finiteness, constructibility, quasi-compactness or boundedness condition.
